question: What does GPU compute cost when weights stream from host RAM over PCIe instead of sitting in VRAM, and is there an offload fraction where a model that does not fit is still worth serving?
arms: --cpu-offload-gb 0 - the control, and vLLM's own default. Every figure this project has was taken here.
--cpu-offload-gb > 0 on a model that does NOT fit the card, swept upward until it serves. srv1's 6144 MiB is the interesting host: it is the one where the question is real rather than hypothetical.
the same model fully resident on srv2's 12288 MiB, as the ceiling the offloaded arm is measured against - so the answer is a fraction of achievable, not a bare tok/s

searched: records/evidence/calibration-2026-08-19/README.md - has per-cell ramp and launch timings, all for fully-resident models
tools/bench/rate-card.json - prices bench tasks in seconds, not serving
tools/power/ - answers required_n, not wall clock
estimate_minutes.why: no run in this repo has ever served a model that did not fit, so there is no measured basis for how long an offloaded load or ramp takes. The first cell of this run is what produces it.

cost.source: no serving rate card exists; see searched above

could_have_carried: DIGEST_TIMEOUT_S - an offloaded model is a large checkpoint, which is the case the 1800 s constant was picked for and never measured against
the spill question DE-G left open: every entry that declared a min_vram_fraction floor read exactly 1.0, so the floor has never gated anything on any entry
left_on_table: ollama's equivalent is not this knob: llama.cpp splits by LAYER (n_gpu_layers on the card, the rest executed by the CPU) rather than streaming weights to the GPU. Testing both would answer 'which degradation is cheaper', which is a different and larger question.

PCIe gen3 x16 is ~15.75 GB/s theoretical, which is BELOW srv1's measured 21.8 GB/s host RAM bandwidth and above srv2's 13.3 GB/s. So on srv1 the link binds and on srv2 the memory may - that asymmetry is not an arm here and would need its own run.
prerequisites: a vLLM model entry larger than srv1's 6144 MiB - the only vLLM entry in tools/bench/serving/configs/srv-full.json is the 1.5B AWQ, which fits everywhere and cannot produce the condition
docker vLLM on both rigs - done 2026-08-22, image sha256:ffb2d59b1c059a5bd8d781320c9f5189de8293693b7d95da54befddaa54abf52 identical on srv1 and srv2
pcie.link.gen.current read UNDER LOAD, not at idle
void_if: the PCIe link is not recorded at the moment of measurement. Read 2026-08-22 at idle, both rigs report gen 1 of a gen 3 maximum at x16 of x16 - the cards downclock the link when idle, so an idle reading describes nothing about a run and a run that records only the idle value has measured an unknown link.
the two rigs' links differ at load and the figures are compared anyway
the offloaded arm is compared against a fully-resident arm on a DIFFERENT card without saying so - srv1 is Turing CC 7.5 and srv2 is Ampere CC 8.6
notes: Filed 2026-08-22 at the owner's instruction, after establishing that 'spilled to CPU' and 'in RAM' are not alternatives: a CPU-executed layer's weights are in system RAM by definition. The thing worth testing is the other shape - GPU compute reading weights across PCIe - which vLLM exposes as --cpu-offload-gb and defaults to 0. Confirmed identical at 0 on both builds by diffing `vllm serve --help=all`: 275 flags, 223 defaults, zero differences.
